Contreras hit .381 with four RBI, had 10 successful ABS challenges and threw out four runners in the triumph over the Rays

        For the first time in franchise history, the Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions, and All-Star catcher William Contreras was named World Series MVP. Contreras went 8 for 21 (.381) and drove in four runs in the five-game series. He struck out once. Contreras also went 10 for 14 in ABS challenges behind the plate and 4 for 9 throwing out basestealers. "I don't have words to say for how I'm feeling," Contreras said through an interpreter following Game 5. "I'm just appreciative of my teammates, appreciative of (manager Pat) Murphy. I want to thank all of them." Contreras became the 27th player in history with multiple hits in each of the first three games of the World Series. That includes a three-hit effort in Game 3. In Game 1, Contreras had two hits and threw out two basestealers. He was an all-around force for the Brewers. Contreras produced at the plate and dominated defensively. "This team's not what it is without this guy," ace reliever Aaron Ashby said after Game 5. "He wants to compete every day. He's our bulldog and we love this dude." 
Contreras had plenty of competition for World Series MVP. Ashby threw 5 ⅔ scoreless innings in the series. Jackson Chourio went 11 for 24 (.458) in the series. Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt went 8 for 19 (.421) and at one point had a hit in four consecutive at-bats spanning Games 4 and 5. All were deserving of World Series MVP honors. The Brewers acquired Contreras in the three-team Sean Murphy trade with the Atlanta Braves and Oakland Athletics in December 2022. That deal has proven to be a heist for Milwaukee. Contreras has emerged as one of the best catchers in baseball and he's gone to two All-Star Games with the Brewers. Now he's World Series MVP. 
Contreras is the first catcher to be named World Series MVP since Salvador Perez with the 2015 Kansas City Royals.

body:
The 2026 Major League Baseball season is over, and the Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time. The Brewers finished off the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday night in Game 5 of the 2026 World Series. MLB Opening Day for 2027 is scheduled for March 24. But whether fans are watching baseball again or not in less than five months is very much up in the air.Major League Baseball's players and owners are in the process of negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement, or CBA. The CBA is the accord that governs the working relationship between the players, as represented by their union, the MLBPA, and the clubs. It covers pretty much every aspect of that relationship that you can imagine, all the way from the overarching salary and payroll structure to daily meal money and days off during the season. Not surprisingly, it's the economic platform of the game that's the toughest to negotiate because that is always, in essence, a fight over money, or how the league's substantial revenues will be divided up between teams and players. That's keenly relevant right now because players and owners are sparring over whether or not MLB will have a cap on salaries moving forward. The owners have renewed their push for a salary cap after not aggressively (or at least not this aggressively) pursuing one since the 1994-95 players' strike. Matters are such that the owners are expected to implement a lockout of the players after the current CBA expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1 of this year.

        
            
                MLB CBA negotiations timeline: Where things stand as Dec. 1 expiration creeps closer
                
                    Dayn Perry                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
What is a lockout?There are two kinds of labor stoppages in MLB: the strike and the lockout. A strike is when the labor side – players as represented by their union, in this instance – puts a halt to operations. A lockout is when the management side – team owners and the commissioner's office doing their bidding, in this instance – initiates the stoppage. In plainspoken terms, a strike is a refusal to work, and a lockout is a refusal to permit work to be done. For those on the outside, the result is the same, in that there's no Major League Baseball during a lockout or strike. What does a lockout mean?When a lockout is in force in MLB, as is expected to be the case after this CBA expires, nothing happens on the major-league front. And we do mean nothing. There's an almost literal element to a lockout in that anyone on the 40-man roster of any MLB club will be locked out of any team facility for the duration of the stoppage. That also means no access to team trainers or team physicians or members of the coaching staff. Beyond that, there's a transaction freeze in place starting the moment the lockout begins (more on that in a moment).
Additionally, MLB is expected to remove player images and videos from the league's official website, MLB.com, and player images and even names would be removed from articles on MLB.com. A league memo acquired by The Athletic also forbids contact between players and anyone on the club side, at least to the greatest extent possible. The latter extends all the way down to a recommendation against sending holiday cards to players who have been locked out. Bottom line: A lockout means the sport at the highest level is on hold across all fronts until further notice. "Further notice" almost certainly means when a new CBA is agreed to in principle and then ratified by both sides.How will a lockout affect free agency and the 2026-27 offseason? As just noted, a lockout means a transaction freeze, which means no players on any 40-man rosters can be traded and no major-league free agents can be signed for as long as the lockout lasts. Free agency, however, begins on Monday (Nov. 2), so there is roughly one month available for those looking to make trades or signings (once the five-day exclusive negotiating window closes and qualifying offers are extended) before the freeze sets in.
It's worth noting that in the run-up to the last lockout of 2021-22, we saw a swarm of free agent signings just before the lockout began. We could see that flurry of moves again, particularly in light of proposed changes to contract structures that would limit lengths and dollar amounts. Would players like Tarik Skubal, who are eyeing mid-nine-figure contracts, want to get their deals done quickly and hope they're grandfathered in?That said, there's a lot more uncertainty about what the game's financial structure will look like after this CBA negotiation concludes, at least relative to the last time we did this. That may have a chilling effect on the trade and free agent markets leading up to the lockout date. Clubs don't like mass uncertainty when it comes to making major roster decisions, and they may prefer to see what the league's salary and revenue sharing systems will look like for the next half-decade (the term of each CBA these days) before committing to signings and trades. If the lockout spans a meaningful amount of time, then that means a great deal of usual winter business will be put on hold. The MLB Winter Meetings and the major-league portion of Rule 5 Draft are typically held in the first half of December, so those could be imperiled. Last time out, the major-league portion of the Rule 5 Draft was indeed canceled, although the November Rule 5 protection deadline had already passed. If the lockout stretches into January, then the exchange of arbitration figures between eligible players and their teams will be delayed. Get well into late January and early February without an agreement, and arbitration hearings and the spring training schedule could be shortened or imperiled altogether. Needless to say, local businesses and elected officials in Florida and Arizona would very much not like that. That, though, could be the least of our worries. 

        
            
                What Rob Manfred and the MLBPA said about salary cap fight as lockout looms over 2026 World Series
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Will this affect the 2027 season?It very well might. It's too soon to say, but there's the real potential for disruption and, perish the thought, maybe even cancellation of the 2027 season. The latter is of course the worst-case scenario, and there's no reason to think there's a strong threat of that possibility, at least this far out. During the last lockout, though, the two sides weren't fighting over quite as much territory, and we very nearly lost games from the regular-season schedule. Lest anyone forget, the last time the owners vigorously pushed for a salary cap, we wound up losing the World Series. There is a wrinkle of note that may make a worst-case scenario less likely. If the lockout drags on long enough to cancel 60 or more games from the 2027 MLB season, then the fallout could be significant. The Athletic recently reported that if the lockout extends into late May or so and costs at least 60 games, then most of the league's national broadcast and streaming contracts would be extended for another year, through 2029. That matters because Manfred and the league hope to bundle and centralize team streaming rights and share those revenues equally, and the current timeline would theoretically allow that to happen at the same time the national contracts are up for renegotiation in 2028. Tacking on another year to those national contracts would push back the significant windfall that owners and the league are expecting from that new media rights structure. This amounts to a major incentive, at least on the league side, to agree to a new CBA before June arrives.And what about the minor leaguers and their 2027 season? Just players on the 40-player roster will be affected by the lockout, as mentioned. While that includes some minor leaguers, the vast majority of minor-league players are not on the 40 and thus will not be impacted. Minor leaguers now have their own CBA independent of MLB players, and that CBA is still in force. Thus, they're not being locked out. The minor-league season will proceed as normal, albeit minus those prospects on their respective 40s, just as it did during the 2021-22 lockout. So, yes, there will be affiliated professional baseball going on even if the lockout stretches into the 2027 regular season. 
Why are we having a lockout in MLB?To hear commissioner Rob Manfred tell it, the lockout is designed to hasten negotiations between the two sides and speed up the process of forging a new CBA that, assuming it arrives in time, will cover the 2027-31 MLB seasons. Manfred cited this very reason leading up to the lockout of 2021-22, and during the drumbeat phase of this approaching lockout, he said this: "In a bizarre way, it's actually a positive. There is leverage associated with an offseason lockout, and the process of collective bargaining under the NLRA (National Labor Relations Act) works based on leverage. The great thing about offseason lockouts is the leverage that exists gets applied between the bargaining parties."After implementing the 2021-22 lockout, Manfred said the drastic decision was designed to "jumpstart the negotiations and get us to an agreement that will allow the season to start on time." Actions, though, hold sway over words, and after locking out the players, MLB owners didn't make their first CBA proposal to the players for another six weeks or so. In reality, the purpose of a lockout is to preempt a strike. The union can time a strike so as to exert maximum leverage and apply maximum pressure on ownership, say, during the stretch drive or soon after Opening Day or just in advance of the playoffs. From a fan and observer standpoint, though, at least this gets the clock started before games hang directly in the balance. Has this happened before? Yes. The forthcoming lockout will be the 10th labor stoppage in modern MLB history – five strikes and, soon, five lockouts. Here's a quick look at the nine lockouts and strikes that have already happened: 
MLB work stoppageDates1972 strikeApril 1-13, 19721973 lockoutFeb. 8-25, 1973 1976 lockoutMarch 1-17, 19761980 strikeApril 1-8, 19801981 strikeJune 12 - July 31, 19811985 strikeAug. 6-7, 19851990 lockoutFeb. 15 - March 18, 19901994-95 strikeAug. 12, 1994 - March 31, 19952021-22 lockoutDec. 2, 2021 - March 10, 2022As you can see, there are occasions in which the stoppage is lengthy and disruptive, and in other instances they barely register. Given the complex nature of the current negotiation, the expectation is that the upcoming lockout won't be resolved quickly. There is, though, some runway between "immediate resolution" and "2027 season greatly harmed." What are the key issues that must be resolved?It's the salary cap, first and foremost. MLB has coveted a capped system for decades, but for the MLBPA, the strongest union in sports, a cap is a complete nonstarter. If the stoppage turns into a war, then it will be because owners continue pushing for a cap and players continue to resist. Let it be known that despite the public narrative, the main advantage of a salary cap for owners is not that it will promote competitive balance, but rather that a payroll cap figures to increase franchise values. Otherwise, changes to the way the league shares local revenues are also up for negotiation. MLB already shares local revenues at significant levels, but Manfred and owners want to share them more equally among teams, perhaps similar to what the NFL does. The good news is that the union has already shown a willingness to discuss such changes and indeed has proposed something similar. That's common ground on a negotiation that figures to need as much of that as possible. As well, increasing the sharing of local revenues, especially local broadcast revenues, would help achieve what the league claims a cap would achieve and do so without a 1994-95 scale of work stoppage.Given the all-encompassing nature of the CBA, many other issues will need to be sorted out. Those may include the length of the regular season, postseason format, the minimum salary, any changes to free agency and salary arbitration, the implementation of an international draft, retention of the qualifying offer system, active roster sizes, draft bonus pools and eligibility, and -- if retained -- the structure of the Competitive Balance Tax system. That's not an exhaustive list, and all of it has to be hammered out, at least in terms broadly agreeable to both sides, for the lockout to end. For now, though, the league hasn't moved off its demand for a cap, and until that changes -- or until the union acquiesces (highly unlikely) -- that issue will determine how long the lockout lasts. Is there any reason to hope the lockout will end before the 2027 season is damaged?Yes, there is. Once we get into spring training and beyond, any continued shutdown costs clubs and players money. MLB owners have a significantly larger war chest than the players do, but neither side relishes missed broadcast and gate revenues or paychecks. As detailed above, there's heavy incentive to get this resolved before the 60-game mark of the regular season because of broadcast contracts. Along similar lines, with attendance continuing to rise and revenues also increasing each year, the game is in a relatively healthy spot. Pace-of-play initiatives are broadly popular among paying customers, as is the implementation of the ABS challenge system. Expansion to 32 teams is probably also on the horizon. All of that adds up to a potentially lucrative glut of national broadcast contracts, and a lockout that cuts the 2027 season to ribbons would do great harm to what may be MLB's most important business-side objective of all right now. The 1994-95 strike also still provides a roadmap to how much damage the "nuclear" outcome can do to the sport. Every labor stoppage is a skirmish over money, but the prospect of losing a hunk of the money they're fighting over can reveal shared interests and the foundations of compromise. Therein lies the hope for those of us on the outside.

A 3-17 record across two seasons and an offense that ranked last in Conference USA proved to be Longo's undoing with the Bearkats
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 28, 2026

    4:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Sam Houston has fired coach Phil Longo after less than two seasons, the school announced on Wednesday. Associate head coach Eric Raisbeck and defensive coordinator Freddie Aughtry-Lindsay will serve as interim co-head coaches for the rest of the season. Longo went 3-17 in two seasons, including 1-11 in Conference USA play. The Bearkats are winless against an FBS opponent and lost 24-3 to Missouri State on Tuesday, their ninth straight against FBS competition. "Phil has contributed to Bearkat football as both an offensive coordinator and head coach, and we appreciate his work with our student-athletes," athletic director Bobby Williams said in a statement. "Our responsibility is to evaluate the program's performance and direction. After careful review, I believe a change in leadership is necessary to position Bearkat football to compete consistently in Conference USA and meet the expectations of our student-athletes, university and supporters." Longo was hired for his first FBS head coaching role only weeks after he was fired as Wisconsin's offensive coordinator, making him a cheap addition for a young FBS program. He was hired to replace K.C. Keeler, who led the Bearkats to an FCS national championship in Spring 2021. Under Keeler, the program went 10-3, with its first bowl win since transitioning to FBS two years earlier. 
Longo worked as an offensive coordinator under Keeler from 2014-16, helping to lead the program to two Southland titles and a national FCS semifinal. But from the start, Longo struggled to find his way with the Bearkats. His signature offense ranked last in CUSA both seasons as a head coach, including a paltry 322.8 yards per game in 2026. The Bearkats scored only three points in three of their four conference games.

title: Dream staying focused and confident ahead of WNBA Finals Game 6 despite scheduling madness - CBS Sports
description: Down 3-2 in the series, Atlanta faces elimination at home on Thursday in a midday showdown against the Valkyries
body:
Down 3-2 in the series, Atlanta faces elimination at home on Thursday in a midday showdown against the Valkyries
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ATLANTA -- While the Atlanta Dream and WNBA play the blame game and the outside world expresses outrage and condemnation over the midday Game 6 of the WNBA Finals, Dream players and head coach Karl Smesko are staying laser-focused on the task at hand: evening the series against the Golden State Valkyries and keeping their hopes of a WNBA championship alive."Funny thing about Atlanta, I knew they were going to show up and show out," Angel Reese told reporters on Wednesday afternoon after practice at Gateway Center, referring to the fact that the game sold out just hours after tickets became available on Monday. "It being sold out is not a surprise to me because I know how much they support us and they've supported us all season. So it is really cool, and I'm really grateful to be able to play in front of the fans one more time."Despite the scheduling debacle turning into a bigger conversation than the basketball itself, Smesko said the team hadn't really even talked about it that much among themselves. "I haven't really heard them mention much about it, so I think we're handling it great," the second-year coach said. "I think we're trying to focus on the basketball and let other people take care of that, and we're just glad that it came to a solution." 
Thursday will be a historic day no matter what. It will be the first Game 6 in WNBA Finals history -- the championship series just switched to best-of-seven in 2025, and the Las Vegas Aces swept the Phoenix Mercury in the first edition. Game 6 was originally scheduled at a more traditional time of 8 p.m. ET. The Dream, though, had only reserved their regular-season home, the Gateway Center Arena, for the playoffs. The problem? The Gateway Center Arena is the smallest in the league, seating only 3,500 fans. Five Dream regular-season games and all previous playoff games were played at State Farm Arena, the 17,000-seat home of the Atlanta Hawks. But last-minute scheduling changes made it possible to host Games 3 and 4 at State Farm, but the Hawks tip off at 8 p.m. at home on Thursday and weren't giving up their arena. That left this Thursday matinee -- 12:30 p.m., to be exact -- as the best option all parties could agree to.But while Dream ownership was calling out WNBA leadership, and others were throwing stones back at the Dream organization, the players had a much more immediate issue to deal with: the Valkyries' defense.
        
            
                Why is a WNBA Finals game starting at 12:30 p.m. on a Thursday? Everything to know as Dream blame the league
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Valkyries and Dream had the top defenses in the league this season, so it's not a surprise that scoring has been tough to come by in this series. But since the Dream won Game 3 97-91 to take a 2-1 lead in the championship round, the Valkyries have absolutely stifled Reese and her team, winning Game 4 in Atlanta 67-62 and Game 5 back in San Francisco 64-55. Reese, who was on fire earlier in the series, was held to just 15 points combined in the last two games. 
Reese, the third-year forward who was traded to the Dream from the Chicago Sky in the offseason and was just named to the first All-WNBA second team of her career earlier this month, said the team had a particularly good film session on Wednesday morning and was ready to come out strong on Thursday and force a Game 7 at the Chase Center on Halloween."We are able to see in film that a lot of these things are just us, like missing shots or turning the ball over, or just not being on our defensive principles," Reese said. "Just kind of figuring that thing out is really just keeping us together. Honestly, [Dream rookie guard Isabele Borlase] said it today; she was like, 'I felt really, really good after that film session,' and that's good coming from a rookie because there could be a lot of pressure, especially going off a two-game losing streak. So everybody's in a great mind space right now."When asked what advice she had for her team heading into such a uniquely timed game, veteran DeWanna Bonner said that time and place were pretty irrelevant.
"I don't think that they need any advice. It's just win or die," she said. "No matter what the timing says, you can't even worry about that because that's the least of our worries. We just need a court, ball, hoop. Once we start feeding into all that, I think that's something the media can do. That's something the fans can worry about. We've got our own things that we got to figure out."Bonner said that despite her team's offensive inefficiency in the series, they planned to keep shooting, no matter what."We haven't lost confidence," she said. "That'd be crazy to lose confidence."

title: 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery odds: Who has the best chance at the No. 1 pick? - CBS Sports
description: We're closer to learning which team will have the ability to potentially draft USC star JuJu Watkins at No. 1
body:
We're closer to learning which team will have the ability to potentially draft USC star JuJu Watkins at No. 1
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery will take place on Sunday, Nov. 15, the league announced Wednesday, and will air at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN after the UConn vs. Louisville women's basketball game. With that announcement, the WNBA revealed the official odds for the new seven-team lottery, headlined by the new edition of the Houston Comets (formerly Connecticut Sun) and the Toronto Tempo, who will split the best odds for the No. 1 overall pick.  The WNBA uses two-season aggregate records to determine lottery odds, but for the two expansion teams, the Tempo and Portland Fire, only their 2026 record will be considered. The Comets (as the Sun) went 22-66 over the last two seasons, while the Tempo were 11-33 in their inaugural campaign.  Because the two teams went 11-33 and had identical .250 winning percentages, the league combined each team's lottery combinations and divided them evenly. There was an even number of combinations, which means the teams will have identical odds for the No. 1 overall pick. If there had been an odd number of combinations, the Comets would have received the extra combination by virtue of losing the tiebreaker last season. In addition to the Comets and Tempo, this year's lottery crew includes the Chicago Sky, Seattle Storm, Phoenix Mercury and Los Angeles Sparks. However, those will not be the seven teams drafting in the lottery. The Sky owe the Washington Mystics a first-round pick swap, while the Mercury traded their first-round pick to the Sparks, who will have two lottery selections as a result. It is important to note, however, that lottery odds are based on the team that originally owned the pick. 
2027 WNBA Draft Lottery oddsTeamCombined 2025 and 2026 recordOdds of winning No. 1 pickComets22-66 (.250) 				32.9%Tempo 				11-33 (.250)* 				32.9%Sky (owe to Mystics) 				26-62 (.295) 				16.1%Storm 				31-57 (.352) 				9.3%Fire 				17-27 (.386)* 				5.2%Sparks 				37-51 (.420) 				2.4%Mercury (owe to Sparks) 				43-45 (.489) 				1.2%How does the lottery work?Here's how the lottery process works, via the league:In the drawing, 14 balls numbered 1-14 will be placed in a lottery machine and mixed.  Four balls will be drawn to determine a four-digit combination.  The team assigned that four-ball combination will receive the No. 1 pick. The four balls will then be placed back into the machine and the process will be repeated to determine the second pick.  Of the five Lottery teams not selected in the drawings, the team with the worst cumulative winning percentage shall select third; the team with the next worst records will, in order, select fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh.A representative from the league's independent accounting firm Ernst & Young will be in attendance to oversee the Draft Lottery process.Houston was 1-2 against Toronto in the 2026 regular season (the first tiebreaker) and, therefore, cannot fall further than the third pick. Toronto is guaranteed at least the fourth pick.Top WNBA prospects to watchUSC star JuJu Watkins is the player to know in the upcoming NCAA season. The 6-foot-2, do-it-all wing will make her return after missing all of last season with a torn ACL. And despite her injury, she is the clear favorite to be selected No. 1 overall in the 2027 WNBA Draft. Of course, that assumes that she declares. Because she took a medical redshirt last season, she's eligible to return to school for a fifth year in 2027-28. 
        
            
                2027 WNBA Mock Draft: USC's JuJu Watkins goes No. 1 to Comets as franchise embarks on new era
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Watkins is not the only talented prospect in next year's class. Texas forward Madison Booker and Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo also stand out and are likely top picks. Kansas guard S'Mya Nichols, LSU guards Mikaylah Williams and MiLaysia Fulwiley and Kentucky center Clara Strack are other lottery candidates to keep an eye on. 
On the international scene, French teenagers Sarah Cissé, the 2026 U20 EuroBasket Women MVP, and Aïnhoa Risacher, the younger sister of former NBA No. 1 overall pick Zaccharie Risacher, are potential first-round picks.

title: Brewers win the 2026 World Series: Where the Brew Crew ranks among the best recent MLB champions - CBS Sports
description: The Brewers just put together a historically great season and won the first World Series in franchise history
body:
The Brewers just put together a historically great season and won the first World Series in franchise history
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ST. PETERSBURG -- The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions. There's so much weight in such a statement on its own, but let's consider for a second all the context behind it. The 2026 Brewers won 103 games in the regular season and then, more impressively, went a ridiculous 11-2 in the playoffs, never facing elimination, never even trailing in a series. They were one loss away Not only that, but they came so close to being the first team ever to go 8-0 in the League Championship Series and World Series. The 1976 Reds were the only team to sweep both the LCS and World Series, but that only got them to 7-0 because the LCS was five games until 1985. The best playoff record in the era of multiple wild cards was the 2022 Astros at 11-2, and the Brewers have tied that. The 2005 White Sox went 11-1 and so did the 1999 Yankees. We're already up in rarefied air. But there's more.Think about how hot the Brewers closed. They finished the regular season by winning 15 of their last 18 games. This means they went 26-5 after Sept. 6. Further, look at who they decimated in the playoffs. The Padres were riding a run of 19 wins in 22 games, including a two-game sweep in the Wild Card Series. The Brewers went 3-1 in that NLDS. The Dodgers were the two-time defending champions who swept the Brewers in the NLCS last year. They won 100 games in 2026. The Brewers swept them in four games. The Rays won 98 games in the regular season and were 7-2 thus far in the playoffs. The Brewers took them down in five with their only loss coming in 12 innings. Remember the Bob Uecker line from "Major League?" There's nothing left but a vapor trail. 
That's the Brewers' path to the championship. They just became an absolute killing machine down the stretch, pulverizing everything in their path. Statistically, they can't touch the 1998 Yankees (114 wins, +309 run differential, 11-2 playoff record including World Series sweep) and certainly can't get to the 1927 Yankees (110-44, +376 run differential, swept World Series). But what about more recently?Such an exercise is subjective, but let's figure out where these Brewers rank in recent memory. Probably really close to the top, if not all the way up. This wasn't a team loaded with future Hall of Famers, as the Dodgers were last season, for example, but the numbers say these Brewers take a back seat to very few, if any, teams in the past couple of decades. 
In fact, let's sort through it. I'll go with the multiple-wild card era, so we're starting in 2012. Let's narrow it down to teams that won at least 100 games and also won the World Series. Yes, the World Series title is a requirement, so we can safely say goodbye to the 2021 Giants and 2022 Dodgers. We'll compare the teams via regular-season record, run differential, playoff record and how they fared in the World Series. As you'll see, the Brewers will have the most impressive resume here. Five teams qualify: TeamRegular season recordRun differentialPlayoff W-LWorld Series result2016 Cubs103-58-1+25211-6Won in 72017 Astros101-61+19611-7Won in 72018 Red Sox108-54+22911-3Won in 52022 Astros106-56+21911-2Won in 62026 Brewers103-59+21411-2Won in 5
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2016 Chicago Cubs An absolute juggernaut in the regular season outside of a wretched stretch before the All-Star break, the Cubs finally broke the faux curse and won it all. They had the regular-season MVP and two Cy Young candidates, in addition to the Cy Young winner from the previous year. On the downside of this argument, they trailed in both the NLCS and World Series (three games to one). Coming back is impressive, but the most dominant teams didn't fall behind.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2017 Houston AstrosThe first World Series title in franchise history came with a young and (at least it felt like it at the time) fun team. They had the MVP and a former Cy Young winner and also traded for future Hall of Famer Justin Verlander. They needed seven games in both the ALCS and World Series.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2018 Boston Red Sox The highest win total on the list is right here. They also never faced elimination in the playoffs, though they did trail 1-0 in the ALCS. The MVP of the league was again on the champs and they also had three Cy Young winners (Chris Sale hadn't won his yet, but he was the undisputed ace). 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2022 Houston AstrosAfter a 106-win regular season, the Astros steamrolled through the American League side of the bracket, going 7-0. They did lose Games 1 and 3, though, to fall behind 2-1 in the World Series after seeing the Phillies club them for a bunch of home runs in a 7-0 Game 3 win. The Astros righted the ship thereafter, though, and won the next three games, including two nail-biters. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2026 Milwaukee BrewersThough the regular seasons are pretty comparable in that chart above, the Brewers were easily the top dog in the postseason. They lost one game between the NLCS and World Series. Any other teams worth considering?We should probably loop in the 2013 Red Sox, the 2015 Royals and the repeat champion 2024-25 Dodgers as well. Red Sox (2013): They tied for the MLB lead with 97 wins in the regular season and then went 11-5 in the postseason, never facing elimination. David Ortiz went 11 for 16 with two doubles and two homers in the World Series. Still, they trailed in both the ALCS and World Series.Royals (2015): Behind incredible defense and a dominant bullpen, the Royals won 95 games and took down the Mets in five games in the World Series. Somewhat similar to the 2026 Brewers, it felt like every time they got behind, the Royals were going to come back. They just weren't as good. Dodgers (2024-25): Funnily enough, in the last seven full regular seasons, the Dodgers won at least 100 games five times. The two times they didn't, they won the World Series. The 2024 squad won 98, but the rotation was patchwork by the World Series. How about the '25 bunch? They "only" won 93 games in the regular season, then went 13-4 in the playoffs. The star power of Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Mookie Betts is a bonus. How about the rotation? It was ridiculous, as Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow and Ohtani looked like a group of Cy Young winners. This team is definitely in the mix. But is that enough?The verdictIf I had to rank them, I think the Mount Rushmore in this era would be: 2018 Red Sox2026 Brewers2022 Astros2016 CubsThe 2025 Dodgers were a tough omission, but they didn't even earn a bye due to a relatively low regular-season win total. I'm willing to hear arguments for the Brewers over that Red Sox team, too. After all, the Red Sox did lose a whole three playoff games, even though they never faced elimination. The bottom line is that the 2026 Milwaukee Brewers are one of the best, if not the greatest, champions in recent history.

title: What's next for the Rays? Three questions after World Series loss, including payroll and Junior Caminero - CBS Sports
description: The Rays fell to the Brewers in the 2026 World Series; will they be back in contention in 2027?
body:
The Rays fell to the Brewers in the 2026 World Series; will they be back in contention in 2027?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Tampa Bay Rays' 2026 season is over. Coming off a 98-win regular season, the American League East title, and their third-ever pennant, the Rays were eliminated in five games from the 2026 World Series by the juggernaut Milwaukee Brewers. There's pride to be taken in the Rays' overall body of work this year, but the prevailing reality is that they failed to achieve their ultimate goal. While the Brewers are celebrating their first World Series title, the Rays remain on the list of franchises that have never hoisted the trophy. This all means that the Rays now turn their attention to 2027 and whether they're likely to make another run at relevance, contention, and perhaps another bite at the championship apple. Let's explore that now by exploring three questions that will define the Rays' coming offseason and their 2027 campaign. 1. Will ownership raise payroll?The Rays, across so much of their history, have reliably punched above their weight. The foundation of that has been a level of support and investment from club ownership that's been entirely lacking. The present ownership group, led by Jacksonville real estate something or other Patrick Zalupski, took over in September of 2025, so this is almost wholly an indictment of former owner Stuart Sternberg. Since the Rays' current run of contention began with their 90-win campaign in 2018, the club has never ranked higher than 24th in Opening Day active roster payroll and never higher than 22nd in luxury tax payroll (basically 40-man roster payroll based on average annual value of contracts). Twice in that span, the Rays have ranked last in year-end 40-man payroll. Given that the current revenue-sharing structure gives small-market teams more than enough to cover cash payrolls, this is all a plain dereliction of duties on the part of Sternberg. One of the canniest front offices in all of sports and the rosters they have assembled deserve more buy-in from ownership. 
Maybe now that Zalupski's group is in charge and the Rays finally appear to have a new ballpark – heavily funded by tax dollars – across the finish line, things will change on this front. It'd be a fine time for that, given that the Rays right now are self-evidently capable of vying for a title. This winter, they have a number of key contributors due for arbitration raises, including Shane McClanahan, Jonathan Aranda, Griffin Jax, and Bryan Baker. Yandy Díaz in August triggered a $13 million vesting option for 2027, which, based on prior organizational behavior, might make him a trade candidate. There are also a number of investments needed in the rotation, which we'll get into below. There's also the matter of what the next collective bargaining agreement will look like once one is agreed to and the forthcoming lockout ends. Signs point to the next CBA being of benefit to teams like the Rays, and that may inform some of their offseason behavior before that owner-implemented lockout likely begins on the night of Dec. 1. 2. What will the rotation look like in 2027?The need for better stewardship from owners will be acutely critical to the makeup of the 2027 rotation. McClanahan's incoming arb raise – which will likely give him the highest salary of any Rays arb-eligible player this offseason — makes him a trade candidate. Freddy Peralta, their stabilizer after he was acquired leading up to the trade deadline, is a free agent. Drew Rasmussen has an $8 million option/$500,000 buyout for 2027. It should be a no-brainer to exercise said option, but, well, you know. There's also Nick Martinez, who has a $20 million mutual option for next season. That likely means he's headed for free agency, but the Rays should still pick up their end of it on principle. That's 80% of the rotation, at least as it was constituted after the trade deadline and before McClanahan's forearm injury. In all, that quartet of starters combined for a 3.03 ERA during the regular season and 42 of the team's 54 quality starts. They also combined for a WAR of 11.2, and that's despite getting just 10 starts from Peralta. 
The Rays will need to do a lot of retention work on this front if they're going to again be the best team in the American League next season. As it stands right now, the rotation is the biggest unknown going into the offseason. 3. Has Junior Caminero reached his ceiling? The 23-year-old third baseman and emerging superstar is the lineup fulcrum for Tampa Bay. Since his rookie season of 2024, Caminero has improved his OPS+ from 105 to 130 to 144 this past season. His WAR has swollen from 0.7 in 43 games as a rookie to 4.3 in 2025 to 5.7 in 2026. 
He hits the ball exceptionally hard, and he has the fastest bat speed in the game. Additionally, Caminero in 2026 made impressive strides in terms of his plate discipline. Prospects these days, thanks to developmental and training advances at the lower levels, are arriving more ready than ever, and some start off at their peak. Caminero, though, has shown improvement on a number of forward-looking fronts, and that raises the compelling possibility that he still has some growth in him. Is a 50-homer season and an MVP award in the offing? That seems quite possible, and given the unbalanced nature of the Rays' lineup, they could use even more from their best player.

title: The 2026 Brewers were the team of destiny all along -- and now they're World Series champions - CBS Sports
description: After being swept in the NLCS last season, the Brewers dispatched of everyone in dominant fashion in 2026
body:
After being swept in the NLCS last season, the Brewers dispatched of everyone in dominant fashion in 2026
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Since the 2026 playoffs began, we've been using words like "relentless" and "inevitable" when it comes to the Milwaukee Brewers. As they finished their coronation in Game 5 with a 4-1 victory over the Rays to take the series and win their first title in franchise history, it's pretty clear that the Brewers were the team of destiny from early in the season.  Game 5 on Wednesday never really felt like the Rays' night. Their pitching situation was dire after needing to use Nick Martinez in Game 4. The offense was dealing with Jacob Misiorowski and a full Brewers bullpen of studs. Junior Caminero was compromised and Yandy Díaz would join him. It just never felt like it was going to be their night and it wasn't, because of course it wasn't. It was the Brewers' night. The Brewers' series. The Brewers' season.  It took some longer than others to see it, myself admittedly included. They struggled in two different spans in April, with a six-game losing streak and later a four-game losing streak. That was about it, though. After a loss on May 4 dropped them to 18-16, the Brewers went absolutely bonkers the rest of the season: 85-43. And now they've completed an 11-2 playoff run against stacked competition. That means they finished 96-45. Holy smokes. It's a misnomer to act like this is some ragtag bunch; a motley crew, island of the misfit toys collection of big-league players. The Brewers have stars. They have a former MVP in Christian Yelich and, though he's past his prime, he was a quality contributor in the playoffs. Jacob Misiorowski is going to win the National League Cy Young. Jackson Chourio is an emerging superstar. William Contreras is an All-Star catcher. Brice Turang is arguably the best second baseman in baseball. 
The Brewers are such a well-rounded bunch and the front office thrives on winning on the margins, which is why some might slap inappropriate labels on them, such as the little engine that could. That doesn't begin to cover it. They are, in fact, a team of destiny getting contributions from all over the place.  Cooper Pratt had a whopping four hits in Game 4, including a game-tying double in the fourth inning. And, of course, he hit the home run in the top of the 12th inning. Even in a Brewers loss, that game and this series has served as a coming-out party for the youngster who the Brewers have locked up through 2033. He had the go-ahead hit in Game 2. He had two hits and two RBI in Game 5. He was all over with winning plays.David Hamilton hit a game-tying home run in Game 4 from the nine-hole in the lineup and then an RBI single in Game 5. He was acquired from the Red Sox in the deal that sent Caleb Durbin to Boston along with Shane Drohan -- who also contributed in the playoffs -- and Kyle Harrison. Robert Gasser squared off against former Brewers ace Freddy Peralta in Game 3, facing the minimum in his six scoreless innings of one-hit ball. Gasser started the season in the minors. Sal Frelick only had four regular-season home runs and hit the game-tying shot in Game 2. What can we even say about the bullpen? The entire group was dominant, but especially Aaron Ashby, Abner Uribe, Trevor Megill, DL Hall and JoJo Romero. Ashby was the star here, but the entire group was great. Credit Antonio Senzatela with some big outs, too.Garrett Mitchell hit the go-ahead home run in Game 4 of the NLCS to help the Brewers sweep the Dodgers. Who could forget the Jake Bauers story? He was ready to retire from baseball and decided his family needed to stay on the insurance. He won NLCS MVP.There are more examples, of course. It was just a team full of winners. No matter what obstacle popped up for the Brewers this season, and especially in the playoffs, they reacted by winning. For crying out loud, they scored eight runs with two outs in the World Series. That was off-the-charts outrageous in Game 3.Then there were the injuries. Yelich and Chourio missed time. Quinn Priester was lost for the season in spring training. Brandon Woodruff missed most of the year before making the World Series roster. With these injuries, in addition to the trade of Peralta, the door was open for players like Drohan, Gasser and Logan Henderson to make the most of their opportunities.  
That's just what happens with teams of destiny. It's that ol' "next man up" mentality. The Brewers have been practicing this for years, trading away established veterans before they reach free agency and immediately replacing them with inexperienced players or even retreads like Jake Bauers who are ready to step in. For every player out the door, there's someone else ready to shine.The Brewers just won 11 playoff games and came from behind to win six times. That's beyond ridiculous. Overall, teams scoring first in the playoffs were 27-13. Milwaukee accounted for six of the losses in there, bludgeoning its opponents even after falling behind.The "destiny" thumbprints were all over this series. Even in their Game 4 loss, they just kept coming. And they responded to that loss by getting ace-level work from Misiorowski in Game 5 and putting up run-scoring rallies in three of the first six innings. They didn't need any home runs. They strung together winning plays on singles and doubles and sacrifice flies. They can win on home runs, too, as they've done a few times this postseason. They just find ways to win, almost every time. Their starters, bullpen, defense and clutch hitting are just too good. That's what it takes to win, and the Brewers won it all.
I mentioned the early struggles at the start of the season. They closed in opposite fashion. Including the playoffs, the Brewers were 26-5 after Sept. 6. They had established themselves as the best team in baseball from May 4 until early September, and then went into overdrive. How is it even possible for a 103-win team to level up and get better? Relentless. Inevitable. The team of destiny. Milwaukee Brewers, World Series champions.

title: Harry Kane 'still processing' Ballon d'Or win, so he went back to the only thing he knows - CBS Sports

body:
Kane won the Ballon d'Or on Monday, becoming the first English player to pick up the accolade in 25 years and the first Bundesliga player to do so in 30
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MUNICH – Less than an hour into a casual second-round cup match, a pocket of Bayern Munich fans in one corner of the Allianz Arena had moved on from reveling over Michael Olise's brace against second-division side Magdeburg. Their attention was instead on the group of substitutes who were warming up behind the opponent's goal and one person in particular."Ha-rry! Ha-rry!," they called.It was a likely place for Harry Kane to spend a Wednesday evening, no matter the circumstances. Considering Bayern's relative strengths, the coaching staff had already hoped to give Kane the night off, especially with Borussia Dortmund awaiting this weekend and a trip to Atletico Madrid in the UEFA Champions League coming up on Tuesday. This was no ordinary midweek cup game, though, the pre-match guard of honor from his teammates as clear a sign as any of the occasion. It was Kane's first time back since winning the Ballon d'Or on Monday, doing so in his hometown of London.The warm-ups were the only glimpse the crowd got of him on Wednesday, Bayern getting business done swiftly with a 6-1 win. Yet, Kane's appearance on the sidelines alone was celebratory, both after becoming the first Englishman to win the individual accolade in 25 years and the first player from the Bundesliga to do it since Matthias Sammer accomplished the feat in 1996. It was the type of thing that required an afterparty that allegedly stretched long after a delayed, bloated ceremony came to an end at around 11 p.m. local time, though Kane insisted he "didn't party too hard." It also allowed him to follow up a crowning achievement the only way he knows how – "straight back to work."Kane trained on Tuesday and would have been ready to play if called upon on Wednesday, and is expected to prepare as usual for Saturday's clash with Dortmund. It comes as little surprise for a player who has rarely chased individual accolades. He has repeatedly insisted that his goal every four years is to win the World Cup with England, not the golden boot and left boyhood club Tottenham Hotspur for greater collective opportunities with Bayern in 2023 despite being just 47 goals behind Alan Shearer's Premier League goalscoring record at the age of 30. The spotlight has followed Kane for much of his career but he has always chosen to share it. There is no flexibility with the attention the Ballon d'Or carries, though; only one person can win it, no matter how team-oriented that person happens to be.
"It's strange," Kane said. "It's not my normal thing to enjoy. Even the guys, when I was walking out to warm up and they're all there clapping. I don't know. I get quite, maybe, embarrassed by it, but I know this is a big deal and I felt that obviously in the event, I felt that since with the reception and how much messages I've got from not just friends and family but people sending my number to other coaches and people just that have known me or know of me and they all wanted to just say well done. I think I'm still processing everything, to be honest, but look, I know it's a really big deal so I appreciate everyone, and you know, even on Saturday, I know we're going to do something before the game and all this, and it's important to do because it's a big celebration as well."Even in his hometown on Monday, surrounded both by loved ones and his Bayern teammates who chanted his name in the London Palladium as Ronaldo revealed he had won the sport's ultimate individual prize, Kane felt out of place."A lot of nerves and just different emotions compared to a football match or anything like that and a lot of waiting around and just trying to picture what it'd be like if I did win but honestly, just really special," he said. "The support I've had from friends, family, fans, text messages, social media has just been overwhelming almost."
There is a lot Kane has not considered about life post-Ballon d'Or, either, like where the trophy might rest or what will come of the gold-flaked schnitzel that was made by a Bavarian restaurant and delivered to his home."I didn't actually eat it yesterday," he said. "With the match being today, I have a routine of what I eat and stuff but now, obviously, I appreciate it. It's a nice tradition that we have so to have a gold one, let's just keep them coming."True to form, Kane has found the most comfort in a busy week in a return to his familiar routine.
"I think just being back to football," he said. "It feels like the Freiburg game [on Sunday] was six weeks ago. So much has happened in 48 hours. It was nice just to be back. A bit of normality, seeing the fans, getting a reception before the game, obviously, and then honestly just being back with the boys and just watching football and watching the boys play again so it's been a whirlwind of a 48 hours, and it's nice to just kind of be here and feel at home again."He admitted he needs to add a new item to the routine at home, though – protecting the Ballon d'Or from his four children, aged nine to three."My wife and kids are still in London right now," he noted. "They get back on Friday so I haven't actually seen my kids since I won. I spoke to them, obviously, on FaceTime and stuff so I'm excited to see them and show them the trophy. I know they'll be trying to play with it and pick it up and it's quite heavy and so I might have to keep an eye on it this time but normally, the two boys, especially, just smash the ball around and then whoever wins picks up the trophy that I bring home but I'll have to explain it's a little bit more precious, so we'll have to keep an eye on it."

Which players really stood out, for better or worse?

        Welcome to the UWCL Star Power Index -- a look at players who are generating buzz around the UEFA Women's Champions League. Here we will highlight players who have made an impact on games, positive or otherwise. Buzz can come in all kinds of ways, and that means that players on this list are getting attention for one reason or another. This is not a ranking. The players listed are in no specific order; they're just driving the conversation around the game in their own way. If you're following along, you can check out our previous Star Power Index Now onto the latest index update:1. Lily Yohannes (OL Lyonnes)Among a handful of U.S. women's national team players currently injured or benched with clubs active in the Champions League, there is a player who shines just a bit brighter at the moment. OL Lyonnes midfielder Lily Yohannes is back in the Star Power Index after a stellar performance against Inter Milan. She was part of a midfield trio alongside Melchie Dumornay and Damaris Egurrola that dominated the middle third of the pitch against the tournament debutants.Shortly before the hour mark, Dumornay's attempt on goal had just been ruled out after a foul on the play, and the heads-up quick play by the 19-year-old Yohannes resulting in scoring a crazy long-distance lob that chipped the goalkeeper. It's her second chipped goal in the tournament, and it just adds to OL's stacked attack. 
2. Wieke Kaptein (Chelsea FC) Chelsea FC needed a defining game at the midway point of the season, and they got it thanks to a standout performance by Wieke Kaptein The Dutch international ultimately dictated the 2-0 victory and cranked up the energy in the second half. Most of the attacking play ran through Kaptein who was able to pick out runners in the buildup and find space between Roma's lines with deep passes. 
She set up both assists on goals Ellie Carpenter and Kadeisha Buchanan, following up her lone goal game-winner performance against Austria Wien on opening day. The win now gives Chelsea seven points and  puts them among the top four of the league phase table.
3. Gloria Marinelli  (Servette FCCF)Desperate for points and goals, Servette showed up against OH Leuven. Forward Gloria Marinelli turned around the club's Champions League fortunes within the first half, as Servette defeated OH Leuven 5-1 on matchday 3. Paola Hernandez and Joana Marchao added to the ballooned scoreline, but Marinelli set the tone before halftime.The Italian international scored in the 38th minute and again just six minutes later, despite more chances created by OH Leuven. Servette's attack was far more ruthless, all capped by Marinelli's quick brace. It's the first win for the Swiss side, and a crucial three points at the halfway mark of the competition.
Fans can watch all the action across CBS Sports platforms. Paramount+ will live stream matches all season, while select fixtures also broadcast on CBS Sports Golazo Network and CBS Sports Network.4. Marie-Antoinette Katoto (OL Lyonnes)As impressive as Lily Yohannes' goal was against Inter Milan, a win for OL Lyonnes was all but decided by Marie-Antoinette Katoto. The forward started the goal scoring and truly set the tone for OL's big night. After a goalless draw against Chelsea during matchday 2, the striker scored twice in the first half. Her first-half brace puts her in the lead for the Golden Boot race with five goals, and helps OL with a whopping 14-goal differential in the league phase standing.
5. Alessia Russo (Arsenal)There are plenty of questions around Arsenal and why the roster has struggled with unlocking defenses lately. But those questions will have to exclude Alessia Russo because she's been the answer to goal scoring for the Gunners lately. Already riding the momentum of a North London darby against Tottenham in the WSL, Arsenal carried the good vibes into a UWCL performance against Benfica, and Russo's three goals against Benfica puts her scoring streak at seven goals over six matches for Arsenal.
Her completed hat trick, is her first ever in the Champions League, and she recorded her 24th UWCL goal on a penalty conversion. The accomplishment makes her the all-time leading English scorer in UWCL history, surpassing Fran Kirby's previous record of 21 goals.

title: Pressure mounts on Ruben Amorim's AC Milan after 4-2 home defeat ahead Inter clash - CBS Sports
description: The Rossoneri lost 4-2 at San Siro against Bologna ahead of a key weekend of Serie A soccer
body:
The Rossoneri lost 4-2 at San Siro against Bologna ahead of a key weekend of Serie A soccer
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This is not what AC Milan needed ahead of the Derby della Madonnina that will take place on Saturday at San Siro: The Rossoneri lost 4-2 in Milan against Bologna, conceding three goals in the second half after being up 2-1 at the end of the opening 45 minutes. Former Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim faces increasing pressure on his position, as the Rossoneri are already seven points behind the Serie A leaders, Inter and Lazio. Raffaele Palladino's Bologna started off well with the opening goal scored by Samuel Mbangula followed by the early comeback of the home team, with a brace of Alphadjo Cisse, the biggest and most positive surprise of this start of the campaign. However, the advantage only lasted a few minutes in the second half, when Davide Bartesaghi's own goal completely changed the direction of the match in Milan. Later, Mbangula completed his personal hat trick and the game ended 4-2. 
There are multiple issues AC Milan are facing right now. First of all, as Amorim said after the game, AC Milan lacked of energy in the second part of the game, something that many teams are facing right now across Europe, especially considering the schedule and the amount of games played every week. The issue is how AC Milan are handling those moments in the game, seeming incapable of figuring out when to slow down and keep more ball possession, to avoid what happened on Wednesday against Bologna. 
Speaking to DAZN Italy after the match, Amorim seemed worried about the physical condition of his players: "So many games, so many players out, a bit of fatigue set in. We even had a chance to equalise with Camarda, but we didn't manage it. A coach who's been in charge for two months can't expect the whole team to play a different game for ninety minutes, and that's something you should understand. I think we lacked energy, and since we can't rotate as often, it's difficult for us to consistently press and play our football. When we stop playing our football, we suffer." Speaking on the Derby della Madonnina against Inter that will take place on Saturday, Amorim added: "Obviously, we'll try to win the next game. I'm not here to make excuses; I want a team that's always improving, and I'm convinced we can do that. We're Milan, and we always have to win. Tomorrow we'll figure out who will be playing and how to prepare for the match. We'll make all the necessary assessments and prepare as best we can, even though we don't have much time."
AC Milan will host Inter on Saturday in Milan, a key match that can become the last chance for Amorim to convince club owner Gerry Cardinale he was the right choice in the summer, when the American businessman decided to replace the coach and the whole sporting hierarchy. That's a decision that, for now, doesn't seem to have pay off with the appointment of Amorim, but a game like the one against Inter can completely reshape AC Milan's ambitions and change the status of Amorim at the club. If that doesn't happen against Inter, we can't rule out the chances of more changes in the near future at the club.
